title: Environment-aware release automator with signal-led rollback gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Build a release automation component ('Release Automator') that executes canaries, A/B experiments, and shadowing across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments while enforcing environment-specific constraints and triggering deterministic auto-rollbacks based on telemetry signals.

Background: Current rollout tooling assumes a single execution model; differences between Hosted (ephemeral, multi-tenant), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, capacity-aware), and Private (VPC, stricter network/KMS constraints) lead to manual work and occasional configuration drift. We need an operator that understands those differences and applies safe rollout patterns without losing parity guarantees for critical config (routing, model variants, quantization profile).

Scope:
- Implement a policy fabric that maps high-level rollout intents (canary %, shadow, A/B split) to environment-aware execution plans.
- Integrate with telemetry engine to evaluate guardrails (latency p50/p99, error rate, output-quality regressions from evaluation probes) every evaluation window and decide continue/hold/rollback.
- Support tenant-aware sharding so Dedicated customers with reserved pools see deterministic rollout windows while Hosted can use gradual traffic ramps.
- Provide a small 'config-shim' layer for Private deployments where certain runtime features are opt-in (e.g., KMS integration and in-cluster metrics forwarding).
- Implement an auto-rollback simulator mode to run rollout policies against synthetic failure traces before applying to production.

Design highlights and trade-offs:
- Signal-led decisions: use a weighted signal set (latency, error rate, model-eval delta, token-cost delta) to avoid single-metric flips. Trade-off: complexity vs safety. We choose a bounded voting model (majority of signals with configurable weights) rather than a strict threshold on one metric.
- Canary size semantics: Hosted supports fine-grain percent ramps (e.g., 1% -> 5% -> 20%), Dedicated supports ramp by qps or ticketed windows, Private supports manual confirmation gates. We normalise intent to an observable-driven admission controller.
- Shadow vs canary: Shadow traffic will run where capacity allows; we prioritize shadow runs on Dedicated during low-util windows to avoid impacting SLA. For Hosted, shadowing will use sampled requests to limit cost.
- Config parity: full static parity is infeasible due to network/KMS differences. We will guarantee behavioral parity for routing and model variant selection, and provide explicit diffs for non-parsible settings via the config-shim.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Policy fabric API (2 weeks): language to express canary/AB/shadow intents + environment targets.
2) Execution layer adapters (3 weeks): Hosted adapter (percent ramps), Dedicated adapter (qps/capacity-aware), Private adapter (manual gates + config-shim).
3) Telemetry gates (2 weeks): wire signals from Console SLO streams and evaluation harness; implement voting model.
4) Auto-rollback simulator and chaos harness (1 week): synthetic traffic generator and failure scenarios.
5) Integration tests and runbook updates (1 week).

Acceptance criteria:
- Can schedule a canary rollout that ramps differently per environment from a single API call.
- Telemetry gates trigger 'hold' or 'rollback' within one evaluation window under injected regressions.
- Simulator accurately predicts rollback decisions on canned failure traces at >=90% fidelity.
- Console shows per-environment rollout progress with signal breakdown and suggested remedial actions.

Operational considerations:
- Rate limits: ensure Hosted percent ramps are throttled by per-customer quotas.
- Cost control: shadow traffic sampled strategy and Dedicated scheduling to low-util windows.
- Auditing: every decision recorded in audit logs with rationale (signals and weights).

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives from noisy metrics -> mitigation: smoothing windows and hysteresis + ensemble voting.
- Private environments with no metrics export -> mitigation: config-shim to bootstrap metrics export or require manual gate.
- Over-loading Dedicated pools with shadow runs -> mitigation: capacity-aware scheduler and preflight reservation checks.

Metrics to track post-launch: number of automated rollbacks, mean time to detect regression, false rollback rate, time-to-promotion, customer downtime incidents tied to rollout.

Links and references: design doc, simulator repo, and existing orchestration tickets are attached below.
